good: Baseline to baseline, easy, until you are warm and breathing
Nothing here is fast yet
bad: Skipping this because you feel fine — you are about to sprint

good: Hold the fence, stand tall, let the leg swing freely
Build the range across the ten
bad: Arching the back to throw the leg higher

good: Sit into the bent hip, other leg straight, chest tall
Push back out through the heel
Drive the back hip down before you rotate
Reach the top hand at the sky and look at it
bad: Rotating before the hip has opened

good: Tall hips, strike the ground underneath you, quiet contacts
Rhythm first, height second
bad: Reaching the foot out in front of the body

good: Stiff ankles, knees nearly straight, off the ground as fast as you land
This wakes up the spring you are about to use
bad: Bending the knees and turning it into a squat jump

good: Accelerate smoothly to the top speed of each one, then ease off
The last one should feel fast but relaxed
This is the bridge between warm and sprinting. Do not skip it
bad: Going straight to full effort on the first one

good: Land the split-step already loaded, then explode into the first stride
Stay low for the first two steps before you rise up
Full rest between every one — this is a speed session, not conditioning
bad: Standing tall straight out of the start
Cutting the rest short to get it over with

good: Stand tall, lean forward from the ankles until you have to catch yourself, then run
The lean is what puts you in the right shape — do not bend at the waist
Let the first three steps be long and low
bad: Bending at the hips instead of leaning from the ankle
Stepping to catch yourself before you have really fallen

good: Split-step on the baseline, then one hard push-off to the side and set
The first step goes where you are going, not across your body
bad: Landing the split-step flat and heavy

good: From wide out at the tramline, shuffle back to the middle and set
Stay low the whole way, face the net
Drop-step back three steps, then turn and drive forward to the service line
Open the hip to turn — do not step across yourself
bad: Turning your back on the court
